chitchat: "Clean it, check it, know it. A tool you don't understand will get you killed."
"No smart gear on my shelves. Nothing here has ever once phoned home."
"You draw what you've earned. That's not meanness, it's arithmetic."
"Iron sights. No battery to die, no chip to spoof. Learn them and you'll never be blind."
description: A compact, unhurried woman with reading glasses on a cord and a whetstone never far from her hand. Behind her the shelves run in graded rows, every item cleaned and logged in a hand-kept ledger. She fits gear to people the way a good tailor fits a suit: a long look, a short question, and she knows what you should carry.

bye.text: "Keep it clean." She's already back to her ledger.

carry_accept.text: "Both books balance by the end of the week or I will be unpleasant about it, and I am very good at that."

carry_offer.text:
She turns a page. "I keep two ledgers. One is everything the Watch owns. The other is everything it has lost, and it is shorter, and I take it personally."

"There is a cache under the Fisherman's Green that has been in the second book for a month. It is not dangerous and it is not clever. I would simply like it back where it belongs."

carry_report.text: She takes it, checks it against the page without any visible pleasure, and strikes a line through the entry. Then she looks at the line for a second longer than she needs to.

creed.text: "Everything here works without the grid, without an augment, without a wire to the machine. That's the whole idea." She taps a rifle's iron sights. "The chromed will tell you flesh and steel is obsolete. Then a storm rolls through, their fancy optics die, and it's us still standing, still shooting straight over plain iron. Master the simple thing and nothing can take it from you."

loyalty_accept.text: "Bring the parts back. And bring yourself back." She does not look away as you go, and does not pretend she is doing anything else.

loyalty_offer.text:
The Quartermaster puts a purse on the counter. It is heavier than the errand needs to be and both of you can see that.

"Parts we cannot make. All of it sells on Halcyon Boulevard, and the last of it is behind the clinic counter, and you will be waiting there a while."

She slides the list across.

"They will offer you things while you wait. They are very good at it, they will be kind about it, and there is a discount for anybody who looks like they are thinking it over." A beat. "I am not telling you not to. I am telling you I will be here when you get back, and so will the ledger."

loyalty_report.text:
She counts the parts, and then the change, and then she looks at you — at your hands, at the sides of your throat, at the way you are standing — for a great deal longer than four seconds.

"Right," says the Quartermaster, and writes something in the first ledger.

options.label: What's the philosophy of the shelf?
Let me see what I can draw.
Your cache is on the counter.

root.text: She looks up, marks her place in the ledger with one finger. "So they let you in. Good for you." A measuring glance, head to boots. "I'm the quartermaster. What the Watch trusts you with depends on what you've done for the Watch, but you're inside the door, so let's see what fits."

teach.text:
"I fit gear to people," she says, without looking up from the ledger. "Which means most of my job is looking at somebody for four seconds and knowing what they will do under load. You can learn that. It is not a gift, it is a habit with a very long run-up."

She closes the ledger.

"Senses, and will. Noticing, and not giving in. `train senses` or `train will`, and bring me your hands clean."

a plain wool jumper, elbows patched

name: the Quartermaster
